mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1.5%) indicates accommodative monetary policy that reduces discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of economic regime.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >55% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 1.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate below 4.0% signals tight labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >55% of instances when UNRATE < 4.0, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST > 1100) and retail sales (RSAFS > 470,000) indicates robust consumer demand that accelerates corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in >55% of periods when both HOUST > 1100 and RSAFS > 470,000, or Rank IC for interaction term < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a low-inflation regime (CPIAUCSL < 2.0%), a monthly CPI increase exceeding 0.2% signals the end of disinflation and improved corporate pricing power, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in >55% of instances when CPIAUCSL < 2.0 and CPI monthly change > 0.2, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index (INDPRO > 100) indicates expanding manufacturing output, which serves as a leading indicator of economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >55% of periods when INDPRO > 100, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly nonfarm payrolls increase exceeding 200,000 jobs (PAYEMS change > 200) signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in >55% of instances when PAYEMS monthly change > 200, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of quarterly GDP growth above 1.5% (GDPC1 > 1.5) and housing starts above 1100 (HOUST > 1100) indicates robust economic expansion that drives corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in >55% of periods when both GDPC1 > 1.5 and HOUST > 1100, or Rank IC for interaction term < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in retail sales above its 12-month moving average (RSAFS > 12-month MA) signals strong consumer spending that accelerates corporate revenue growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in >55% of periods when RSAFS > 12-month MA, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
